And somehow, by the end of that extraordinary day, a spoonful of milk had become a global story.

Thirty-one years ago, on September 21, 1995, I came home from school to find that something was strangely different. My aunt, who would diligently wait for me every day and was always the one to serve me lunch, was missing. She was more than just the person who fed me; she would sit with me, tell me interesting stories and make the afternoon feel special.I looked for her everywhere. Finally, the housemaid arrived with my plate of dal and rice and casually told me, “Didi has gone to feed milk to Lord Ganesha.”I was puzzled. What did she mean? After lunch, I called a friend from the landline. She had the same story. Her mother, too, was not at home. By evening, my aunt returned, visibly excited, and told my mother, who had just come back from work, what she had seen.“I took a spoon of milk to feed Ganesha, and the milk disappeared,” she said. My mother looked at her in disbelief. “Really?” she asked. “Really. I saw it with my own eyes,” she insisted, quite overwhelmed with emotions.The news spread fast, Ganesha idols were apparently drinking milk. There were no smartphones, social media platforms, WhatsApp groups or instant notifications to amplify the news.India’s internet had only just arrived, television was still dominated by Doordarshan, and newspapers remained the primary source of next-day news. Yet, within hours, temples were overflowing, milk was disappearing from shops and the story had travelled beyond India.It was not the age of viral news. In fact viral was the world synonymous with just one thing-the infectious disease of influenza. There was no way to immediately search the internet, watch a viral video or check social media posts from another city. Then what caused the spread of this frenzy? According to a contemporary Times of India report Mumbai and several other parts of India were swept by reports that Ganesha idols were accepting milk offerings. The report described the news as spreading “like wildfire” as thousands of devotees rushed to temples.The crucial point was that people did not merely hear the claim. They went to temples and tried it for themselves. Devotees carried spoons filled with milk towards the trunks or mouths of Ganesha idols, and many reported seeing the milk disappear.The episode becomes even more extraordinary when viewed against India's technological landscape in 1995. Public internet access had only just been launched by VSNL in August that year. According to historicalinternet use in India in 1995 stood at just 0.026% of the population.Telephones were also far from universal. India had approximately 11.98 million fixed telephone connections in 1995, equivalent to around 1.24 fixed lines per 100 people.This meant that the mechanisms of mass communication were fundamentally different from those available today. A person could call a relative, but there was no instant group messaging system through which hundreds of people could receive the same information simultaneously. News moved through conversations, local networks, religious communities, radio, television and newspapers. And yet the Ganesha story moved extraordinarily quickly.It would be inaccurate to suggest that India had only Doordarshan in 1995. The country's television landscape had already begun changing. Zee TV had launched in 1992, Star TV had entered the Indian market in 1991 and Sony Entertainment Television launched in 1995. But the explosion of private, round-the-clock news channels that would later transform India's news culture was still years away.Doordarshan nevertheless remained hugely influential . An academic study citing Ministry of Information & Broadcasting figures puts India's television universe in 1995 at approximately 40 million television households and 250 million viewers.There was therefore a very different relationship between an event and the news cycle. Newspapers generally reported what had happened the previous day, television had scheduled programming rather than today's constant breaking-news stream, and there was no digital ecosystem continuously refreshing itself. The Ganesha phenomenon had to travel through people before it could become a mass media story.The reports quickly produced visible consequences. A contemporary Los Angeles Times repor published on September 23, 1995, said millions of Indians had rushed to test the phenomenon and reported that milk had “virtually disappeared” from shops in New Delhi by noon.That detail captures the extraordinary feedback loop created by the phenomenon. People heard that Ganesha was drinking milk, went out to buy milk, took it to temples and offered it to idols. The resulting rush itself became evidence of how seriously the story was being taken.Contemporary reports described crowds gathering at temples, with devotees carrying spoons, bowls and containers of milk.The most remarkable part of the episode was perhaps how quickly it crossed India's borders. Reports soon emerged from Hindu communities in Britain, the United States, Canada, Nepal and elsewhere. A contemporary os Angeles Times report noted that the reports had spread beyond India to Hindu communities in other countries, including Britain and Los Angeles. Hinduism Today later recalled receiving telephone calls and fax messages from different parts of the world reporting similar experiences. Its contemporary account provides a fascinating glimpse into how an international religious community communicated before email, social media and messaging apps became commonplace.The technology may appear primitive by today's standards, but the human network was remarkably effective. Someone in India could telephone a relative abroad, that person could contact a local temple, and within hours another community could be trying the same experiment.The story did not need an algorithm to travel. It travelled through relationships.As the reports spread, scientists and sceptics began examining what devotees were observing. One of the principal scientific explanations involved capillary action and surface tension. Rather than the idol literally consuming the milk, the liquid could move along the surface of the material, creating the appearance that it was being absorbed by the idol.For devotees, however, the scientific explanation did not necessarily invalidate what they had experienced. The same physical observation could be interpreted through very different frameworks: as a religious sign by believers, as a scientific phenomenon by researchers, and as an extraordinary mass social event by journalists.Looking back from the age of smartphones, the 1995 episode is remarkable not simply because of what people believed they were seeing, but because of how quickly the information travelled.India's public internet had only just begun. Fixed telephone connections were limited, television was expanding but had not yet become the 24-hour news environment of today, and newspapers operated on a fundamentally different news cycle. Yet within hours, a local report had become a national phenomenon and then an international story.A telephone call led to another telephone call. A conversation at one temple led to another. Newspapers carried the story forward, television added another layer of coverage and international media transformed what had begun as a local religious phenomenon into a global news story.Calling the Ganesha milk episode the world's first viral phenomenon would be too absolute. Stories travelled internationally long before 1995, through newspapers, radio, television and word of mouth.But the episode offers a remarkable case study of mass communication before the social-media era. Millions of people participated in the same rapidly spreading story without having access to the tools that today make such mass participation almost instantaneous.That is what makes September 21, 1995, worth remembering 31 years later. The question is no longer simply whether Ganesha idols were actually drinking milk. The episode has another story to tell, about technology, faith, communication and human networks.In 2026, information can travel around the world in seconds. In 1995, it travelled from person to person, from telephone to telephone, from temple to temple and eventually from newspaper to newspaper.(All images are AI Generated)
Article Summary: A spoonful of milk had become a global story in September 1995. India's internet had only just arrived, television was still dominated by Doordarshan. There was no way to immediately search the internet, watch a viral video or check social media posts from another city.

NEW DELHI: The large number of notices served to electors under the special intensive revision (SIR) largely stem from a key change made to SIR instructions by the Election Commission, based on its experience during SIR Phase I in Bihar. During SIR in Bihar, the rules required electors to attach documents proving their eligibility to be included in the roll, over a dozen documents were listed as acceptable proof of birth, citizenship and residence, at the enumeration stage itself.However following the uproar over the inconvenience caused to electors who may not have had these documents and thus faced exclusion, the EC revised the rules in Phase 2 covering 12 states/UTs, doing away with the requirement to submit documents with the enumeration form (EF) and instead decided to map the electors with the electoral roll from last SIR. The mapping works with inbuilt algorithms to flag logical discrepancies between the last roll and the enumeration forms, based on which notices are automatically issued.“The logical discrepancy detecting software is agnostic and does not distinguish between a VIP and a common man. The fact that election commissioner. S S Sandhu also got a notice due a discrepancy, where his name was mentioned as S S Sandhu in one place and as Sukhbir Singh Sandhu in another, proves this,” an EC functionary pointed out.“The high number of notices seems to unique to urban centres like Delhi, where the electors may have been a little casual while filling up the EF. Also, the BLOs could have been more meticulous in checking forms at the enumeration stage, as this could have cut down the discrepancies that led to the notices,” said an EC official.“If anyone does not return the EF despite three visits of the booth level officer (BLO) to his address and checking by booth level agent (BLA) of political parties, he is either absent, shifted, dead or duplicate elector and his name is not there in draft roll. ⁠If the received EF are incomplete or gives incorrect information, notices are issued.The official added that notices rarely lead to electors’ exclusion and are resolved the moment the elector presents the proof correcting the discrepancy.“No elector is excluded without a hearing, which must be followed by a speaking order, which can, after the final roll be published, be challenged first before the district election officer and then the chief electoral officer,” said an EC official.“Besides, the option of being added back to the electoral roll remains open in perpetuity. Anyone whose name is left out can always fill up Form 6, along with the declaration, on his mobile to get back into the electoral roll,” the official added.
Article Summary: The large number of notices served to electors under the special intensive revision (SIR) largely stem from a key change made to SIR instructions by the Election Commission. During SIR in Bihar, the rules required electors to attach documents proving their eligibility to be included in the roll. EC revised the rules in Phase 2 covering 12 states/UTs, doing away with the requirement to submit documents.

Article Title: Uttarakhand CM Dhami joins women in traditional Chachani dance during Badrinath visit
Article Text:

BADRINATH: Uttarakhand chief minister Pushkar Singh Dhami on Sunday joined local women in a traditional Chachdance at Bamani village near Badrinath during his visit to the shrine, interacting with residents and getting a glimpse of the region's local traditions.During his visit, CM Dhami also stopped at a local shop in Badrinath Dham, where he savoured milk and jalebi. He interacted with local residents and pilgrims who had arrived at the shrine.The chief minister also attended the Shri Badrinath Katha Mahotsav being organised near the Shri Narayan Swami Temple on Narayan Palace Road in Badrinath.Dhami's visit comes amid a series of religious and cultural activities being held in Badrinath as the second phase of the Char Dham pilgrimage is underway following the monsoon season.Earlier on Sunday, Dhami offered prayers at Shri Badrinath Dham and sought the blessings of Shri Badri Vishal for the prosperity and well-being of Uttarakhand and its people.Speaking about the ongoing pilgrimage, Dhami said the first phase had been historic and set a new record, with approximately 51 lakh pilgrims and devotees having already offered prayers."By the grace of Baba Kedar and all our holy shrines, the first phase of the pilgrimage has been truly historic, setting a new record.Approximately 51 lakh pilgrims and devotees have already offered their prayers, and the second phase of the pilgrimage is now underway following the monsoon season," he said.The chief minister said arrangements had been put in place to ensure smooth travel and convenient darshan for pilgrims, adding that roadwork along the pilgrimage routes was also underway.He also said work on the master plan for Lord Badri Vishal was progressing rapidly, while acknowledging the challenges posed by the limited construction season in the high-altitude region.The visit also coincides with the two-day Devbhoomi Cultural Festival being held in Badrinath on September 19 and 20 under Operation Sadbhavana. The festival, organised jointly by the Indian Army and Chamoli district administration, is showcasing Uttarakhand's folk dances, music, handicrafts, local products and traditional cuisine. Women-led self-help groups, artisans, farmers and young entrepreneurs are also participating in the event.The cultural festival is being held with the theme "Our Heritage, Our Future" and aims to provide a platform for local traditions, products and talent from the border regions while connecting younger generations with Uttarakhand's cultural heritage.
Article Summary: Uttarakhand chief minister Pushkar Singh Dhami joined local women in a traditional Chachdance at Bamani village near Badrinath during his visit to the shrine. He also stopped at a local shop where he savoured milk and jalebi. His visit comes amid a series of religious and cultural activities being held as the second phase of the Char Dham pilgrimage is underway.

Article Text:
Environmental issues have no geographical limitations, said CJI Surya Kant

NEW DELHI: Terming Supreme Court the "banyan tree" of environmental justice for its role in protecting the environment and ecology, CJI Surya Kant Saturday said conservation and development are not in conflict with each other and there is need to maintain balance between them.Addressing the inaugural session of 'The Future of Environment and Climate Dynamics' organised by NGT, he said there are constitutional provisions for protection of environment, but words in a constitution are only seeds which need the nurturing waters of judicial wisdom to sprout into life and SC has played that role."And it is here that SC has stood tall as the banyan tree of environmental justice, with roots deep in our civilisational ethos and branches sheltering the rights of unseen generations. It has over the decades championed the idea that progress without preservation is but a mirage that vanishes in the desert of ecological ruin. Its rulings underscore how safeguarding nature is not an act of altruism but of self-preservation, an investment in the very continuity of life. "Highlighting its proactive approach, he said SC has made the right to a pollution-free environment a fundamental right by reading it directly into Article 21 ."That same pattern has carried us to the present day, where SC recently articulated the idea of 'eco-centric proportionality', postulating that environmental protection must be rigorous yet intelligent enough to engage with the world as it exists. This notion has advanced the most pragmatic approach of permitting development solely in conjunction with enforceable conditions, expert oversight, restoration, compensatory afforestation and accountability."Recent Indian jurisprudence on climate has brought this question into sharper constitutional focus by recognising the adverse effects of climate change can impact fundamental rights of equality, livelihood, health and conditions necessary for meaningful enjoyment of these rights," he added.
Article Summary: CJI Surya Kant said conservation and development are not in conflict with each other and there is need to maintain balance between them. He said there are constitutional provisions for protection of environment, but words in a constitution are only seeds which need the nurturing waters of judicial wisdom.

Article Title: In 2026, an Oregon teen paid $3.07 for a Lakers jacket at Goodwill; Sotheby’s matched it to Wilt Chamberlain’s 1972 Finals run and sold it for $89,600
Article Text:
Wilt Chamberlain. Image credits: Wikimedia Commons

A bargain bin find outside Portland

Verifying a jacket worn by an NBA great

From $3.07 to $89,600 at Sotheby's

AI Representation: A vintage Lakers jacket once worn by Wilt Chamberlain. Image credits: Chatgpt

A find that stands out even among thrift store discoveries

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

In 2026, a nineteen-year-old reseller bought a warm-up jacket from a Goodwill store near Portland, Oregon, for $3.07; the jacket later turned out to be Wilt Chamberlain's 1972 NBA Finals jacket, authenticated by Sotheby's and sold for $89,600 at auction. This is yet another addition to an ever-growing list of items found in thrift stores that have proven to be significant sports memorabilia.Quinn Brown, a nineteen-year-old who had been reselling secondhand clothes for three years, was sorting through used clothes at a Goodwill "By-The-Pound" outlet just outside Portland on January 15, 2026, when he noticed a short-sleeved yellow jacket marked "Chamberlain" on the back had been thrown into the bin, according to OPB. He bought the jacket for $3.07 and initially expected to resell it for only a few hundred dollars, as he had found similarly obscure pieces before, according to KPTV. His highest sale to date had been a Sub Pop record-label shirt for $250, reports MyNorthwest. Brown explained that he remembered seeing a Chamberlain warm-up jacket sell for a five-figure sum years earlier, which prompted him to search for pictures of the same jacket online before posting his own find.Chamberlain, inducted into the Naismith Memorial Basketball Hall of Fame in 1978, is considered to be one of basketball’s all-time dominant players based on statistics from the Naismith Memorial Basketball Hall of Fame. In the Sports Hall of Fame , he continues to break NBA records such as scoring 100 points in one game, grabbing 55 rebounds in one game and averaging 50.4 points per game in the 1961-62 season, all records that have remained untouched for over 60 years. Following Brown's post, Sotheby's experts got in touch with him and managed to convince him to sell the jersey at the auction. Through the use of Sotheby’s photomatching technology, it was concluded that the jersey had been worn by Chamberlain during the finals in the 1971-1972 season when he had defeated the New York Knicks in five games to earn himself the title of the MVP of the finals for the first time in his career.Sotheby's set the pre-sale estimate at $150,000–$250,000, describing it on their website as an incredible piece of memorabilia. The final bid came way under this estimate, landing at $89,600, including buyer’s premium, after 48 bids had been placed. Even so, the final price was still a remarkable return on the original $3.07 price tag of the jacket, something few pieces bought in thrift stores can compare to.There was, in fact, a significant gap between Sotheby's estimate and the final bid, with the jacket landing $60,400 below the low end of its $150,000-$250,000 range. Such shortfalls aren't unusual for vintage game-worn memorabilia, since matching a piece to a specific game or series through photos alone is difficult. Brown's jacket, however, was one of the rarer pieces for which Sotheby's photomatching technology succeeded in linking it directly to the 1971-72 Finals.The prolific career of Chamberlain ensures that anything having any connection with him will be collected by somebody. He set the NBA record for career rebounds, with a total of 23,924 rebounds, was twice champion, with the Philadelphia 76ers in 1967 and with the Lakers in 1972, and is a four-time MVP, as stated by the California Sports Hall of Fame. In this light, a jacket associated with his championship period holds far more rarity value than mere career memorabilia.For Brown, the sale was the ultimate jump forward in his collecting career, as he moved from a lifetime of making little money by reselling things to selling one thing that made him a huge profit on the $3.07 that he spent. This also shows that sometimes the most valuable sports memorabilia can be found in a donation box somewhere, waiting to be discovered.
Article Summary: Quinn Brown, a 19-year-old reseller, bought a warm-up jacket from a Goodwill store near Portland, Oregon, for $3.07. The jacket later turned out to be Wilt Chamberlain's 1972 NBA Finals jacket, authenticated by Sotheby's and sold for $89,600 at auction. Brown had been reselling secondhand clothes for three years.

Article Title: Will Southampton manager Tonda Eckert get banned over the club’s Spygate scandal
Article Text:
Tonda Eckert (via Getty)

Tonda Eckert and Southampton prepare for another punishment

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Southampton manager Tonda Eckert is waiting to learn whether he will be banned by the Football Association over the club’s Spygate scandal. The German coach was charged with misconduct in July after an EFL investigation found that Southampton had arranged spying missions on three Championship clubs.Southampton have already faced major punishment. The club were removed from the Championship play-off final and missed out on a potential £200m ($267m) promotion boost. They were also handed a four-point deduction for the new season. Now, Eckert could face an individual suspension.The FA hearing is expected to decide Tonda Eckert’s fate in the coming days. The 33-year-old has already apologised for his role in the scandal and continues to receive strong backing from Southampton.An EFL disciplinary commission previously found that Eckert had orchestrated a “contrived and determined plan” to spy on Oxford United, Ipswich Town and Middlesbrough before the play-off semi-final.Eckert had maintained that he did not know the actions broke EFL rules. He also said the spying had no impact on Southampton’s performances.Speaking about the difficult summer, Eckert told BBC, “I would lie if I say that the summer has just been easy.Of course, if you care deeply about your profession, about the football club, there’s nothing that prepares you for that. There just isn’t.”The manager also revealed that he had spoken to the FA for almost four hours during its investigation.“I’ve had the chance to sit down and just talk the FA through everything that happened,” he said. “And now it’s up to them to make a decision. I don’t really have any emotions towards that.”Eckert believes Southampton have already suffered heavily because of the scandal.“It’s been a big, big punishment. Absolutely unheard of in the history of sports. And it’s tough for me to say that because it concerns me. I’m judging on myself, not an outside situation. But I’ve asked for forgiveness for what I’ve done. I’ve apologised publicly”, he said.Southampton chief executive Phil Parsons has also urged the FA to consider the punishment already imposed on the club, “We don’t know what the FA will actually hand out,” Parsons said. “It could be a long ban. It could be a short ban. It could be a suspended sentence.”Parsons also confirmed that Southampton could appeal if Eckert receives another punishment.The club has continued to back the manager despite the controversy. Parsons said Southampton had recruited players during the summer with Eckert remaining in charge.The club has also given analyst intern Will Salt a permanent academy role. Salt was photographed secretly filming Middlesbrough’s training session before the play-off semi-final. Parsons said Salt had been through a difficult period but described him as a talented young employee.Southampton’s next league match is against Portsmouth on 11 October. By then, Eckert is expected to know whether the FA will impose an individual ban.
Article Summary: Tonda Eckert is waiting to learn whether he will be banned by the Football Association over the club's Spygate scandal. The German coach was charged with misconduct in July after an EFL investigation found that Southampton had arranged spying missions on three Championship clubs. Eckert has already apologised for his role in the scandal and continues to receive strong backing from Southampton.

Article Title: 'The place that gave you heartbreak will also give you a reason to smile': Elavenil Valarivan finds a reason to smile in Japan
Article Text:
Elavenil Valarivan (Image: IANS)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

PUNE: Four days ago, when Elavenil Valarivan landed in Japan she carried with her, mixed feelings. The shooter had been to the country before and while that experience may not have been memorable, it was certainly the one to not be forgotten.Elavenil, 27, participated in her first Olympics at Tokyo 2021, where she finished a heartbreaking 16th. While preparing for Aichi-Nagoya, flashes of 2021 returned to her mind, but the shooter, older and wiser now, was able to put them aside.“Thoughts of Tokyo Olympics crossed my mind. It was not a pleasant memory, but over the years, I have trained to put the past behind me and focus on the present. I also told myself that I needed to focus on the Asian Games and not the Olympics,” the shooter told TOI.“I was 22 then and if I had to tell something to my 20-year-old today, I would tell her to be patient and trust the process. I will tell her that the place that gave you heartbreak will also give you a reason to smile about and heal the memories of the past,” she said.‘Ela’ emulated her mentor Gagan Narang, who had also won two silver medals at the 2010 Asian Games. While the mentor was first to call her after her victory, he was also the first to give her some valuable advice.“When I was coming here, he had told me to keep an eye on the weather, the typhoon and plan my bus travels accordingly,” Ela said.In her first Asian Games in 2018, Ela had finished 14th in the same event. The Ahmedabad shooter has been in good form for the past two years and along with the form, other positivity around her has also kept in good shape, mentally. “While on the field, it is the technicality that matters the most. We don’t think about anything that can make us emotional. But off the field, it has been a good phase.”I am happy for my coach Neha (Chavan) ma’am to be nominated for the prestigious Dronacharya Award. She has worked very hard for me, and I am very happy that her efforts have been recognized,” she said.
Article Summary: Elavenil Valarivan won two silver medals at the 2010 Asian Games. The 27-year- old finished 16th in her first Olympics at Tokyo 2021. The Ahmedabad shooter has been in good form for the past two years. She has been nominated for the prestigious Dronacharya Award.

Illness and injuries kept taking games away, and the year closed with more questions than answers.The $40 million star has spent the summer insisting the mystery illness is in the past. Now a new assistant coach and the general manager are backing that optimism with their own words, and one of them has a very specific plan for the big man. Media Day arrives on Sept. 28, so the first live answers are close.Kristaps Porzingis has sent the same message all summer. The 2024 NBA champion has said more than once that the "mystery illness" is behind the Latvian, and that a full season feels realistic.The staff now sounds like it agrees. Frank Vogel, the new assistant on Steve Kerr's bench, made it plain. "I'm really excited about putting him in my defensive system," Vogel told Luca Evans of the San Francisco Chronicle. Vogel said the scheme is packed with details he believes in, and that shot-blocking bigs get a lot out of it. He looks forward to putting Porzingis in those spots.On paper, the pairing with Draymond Green stands out. A front line of Porzingis and Green could cause opponents real trouble, particularly if Gui Santos, De'Anthony Melton and rookie Yaxel Lendeborg deliver on the perimeter.Golden State finished 11th in the league on defense last year, and this group projects to be better than average.General manager Mike Dunleavy sees it the same way. The team studied the problem at length, Dunleavy told the Chronicle, looking at how to help and how to do better. The things the staff discussed and worked through, he said, "lean in the direction of him having a healthier year."Camp will offer the first real evidence. Media Day is set for Sept. 28, and the Warriors train at BYU-Hawaii from Sept. 29 through Oct. 3. The team has already signed Nick Boyd, Elias Ralph and Obi Agbim to training camp deals, and the 15-man roster is expected to be final in the first week of October.It is easy to see why the Warriors are welcoming good news. Golden State thought the trade deadline had delivered a key piece, and the closing stretch of the regular season said otherwise.Porzingis missed 16 games over that stretch and played in only 15, thanks to a mix of injuries and illnesses. The Latvian big man was more often out than in, which is a tough way to start life with a new team.The play-in tournament brought a bit of hope and then a setback. Porzingis looked good in the win over the Clippers, a sign of what the Warriors had been hoping to get. Against the Suns, right ankle soreness held Porzingis to 15 minutes in the final play-in loss. Fifteen games to close the regular season, then fifteen minutes in the final play-in game.Golden State opens the preseason against the Clippers in Honolulu on Oct. 4, then starts the regular season against the Lakers on Oct. 21 at Crypto.com Arena.

Article Title: How Jayden Daniels’ mom supported his football ambitions before the Commanders made him the star QB
Article Text:
Jayden Daniels’ Mom Became a Key Figure in the Quarterback’s Journey (Getty Images)

How did Jayden Daniels' mom shape his path to the NFL ?

Why did Jayden Daniels' mom become a certified NFL agent?

Washington Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels was carted off the field Sunday against the Dallas Cowboys after dislocating his left elbow on the final play of the first half, the same elbow he injured last November against Seattle. Commanders head coach Dan Quinn confirmed it was a left elbow dislocation with no fracture, with more imaging scheduled later this week. The timing is brutal. Daniels was in the middle of one of his sharper performances this season before the play fell apart. Now, as Washington falls to 0-2, attention turns back to the man behind the jersey and the woman who made sure he got there.Jayden Daniels' parents, Regina Jackson and Javon Daniels, met while both were students at Cajon High School in California, the same school their son would later attend. Football was always part of the family DNA. Javon is a big reason Jayden got into the sport at all. "When he was born, when he was old enough to walk, you hand him a ball, and I said, 'this is what you're gonna do,'" Javon said at the Heisman Trophy ceremony.But it was Regina who kept the engine running. "My mother has never missed a game," Daniels said on "The Pivot" podcast. "If it's raining out there, she's going to be out there.If it's minus degrees, she's going to be out there standing up the whole time making sure she's cheering me on." That is not hyperbole. From Arizona State to LSU to the NFL Draft, Regina Jackson showed up. Every single time."The word perseverance is that kid Jayden," she said before the Heisman Trophy ceremony. "The patience he has, the resilience to continue day after day, hour after hour, minute after minute, to be the best version of himself — just watching him get up at 5:30 in the morning to be great is really hard to describe."Daniels has been equally open about how much she means to him off the field too. "Nothing gets past my mama," he said. "She reads people and doesn't put people around me that don't benefit me. My mom's support through this journey has been huge."Regina Jackson did not stop at being a fan in the stands. She became an NFLPA-certified agent after passing the exam administered in late July 2024, making her likely the first parent of a top-three draft pick in NFL history to earn that designation. She holds an MBA with a concentration in entrepreneurship and a master's degree in public service administration. This was not a vanity project."Role number one, she plays my mom. From there, she's my business manager, and then also she is a certified NFL agent," Daniels said. As of March 2026, she became his only listed agent after he parted ways with Agency 1 Sports Group. With a contract extension on the horizon, her role has never mattered more.When Daniels suffered a hamstring injury and fans started drawing comparisons to Robert Griffin III, Jackson quickly shut it down on social media: "I wish you would stop manifesting RGIII on my son. Words are powerful and that's all that's talked about." She protects the narrative as fiercely as she protects his circle.Now, as Daniels heads into another injury scare with Washington needing answers fast, his mother is again at the center of the storm. Not watching from a distance. Right there.
Article Summary: Washington Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels was carted off the field Sunday after dislocating his left elbow. Daniels' parents, Regina Jackson and Javon Daniels, met while both were students at Cajon High School. "My mother has never missed a game," Daniels said on "The Pivot" podcast.

Article Title: Why Suchika Tariyal lost despite a draw: How 700g denied India’s MMA fighter a historic final and left her in tears
Article Text:
Suchika Tariyal (Video grab)

From an incident at 12 to the Asian Games podium

Judo, Ju-Jitsu and MMA come together

Poll Vote & Share your view Are you optimistic about the future of Indian MMA after Tariyal historic bronze? Very optimistic, more athletes will rise. Not optimistic, it’s still a niche sport. 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

A historic medal, with a bitter aftertaste

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The medal will go down in Indian sporting history. The manner in which it arrived, however, left Suchika Tariyal in tears.Twenty-four years after an episode of eve-teasing at the age of 12 prompted her to learn how to fight, the 36-year-old from Haryana became India's first Asian Games medallist in mixed martial arts on Monday. But instead of walking away celebrating a landmark achievement, Tariyal was left shattered on the mat after a dramatic semifinal ended in a draw — only for the winner to be determined by a 700-gram difference in the fighters' morning weights.Tariyal and Singapore's Hui Hoon Teo had fought through regulation time and an additional one-minute round without either establishing a decisive advantage. The bout was initially awarded to Teo. The Indian camp challenged the decision, after which the result was changed to a draw.Then came the tiebreak.MMA Sports Federation president Nikhil Kunde told PTI that the winner was determined on the basis of the athletes' morning weigh-in, with Teo around 700 grams lighter than Tariyal. The Singaporean was therefore declared the winner 2-0 and advanced to the gold-medal bout, while Tariyal received bronze.For Tariyal, it was a particularly painful way for her gold-medal hopes to end.She had believed she had done enough to win. Teo had the better of the opening period, but Tariyal fought back strongly in the second. Neither could establish clear superiority in the additional round, although Tariyal managed to take her opponent down just as the buzzer sounded.When the final decision was announced, Tariyal struggled to contain her emotions. She broke down in tears on the mat as her coach tried to console her. She did not immediately go across to shake hands with Teo or the referee.The disappointment was understandable. A few moments earlier, the Indian camp had succeeded in getting the initial verdict changed to a draw. Yet the revised result still did not take Tariyal into the final. A difference of roughly 700 grams ultimately separated the two fighters.And yet, history had already been made.MMA is making its Asian Games debut at Aichi-Nagoya 2026, and Tariyal's bronze is India's first-ever medal in the discipline. Her achievement also adds another chapter to one of the most unusual combat-sports journeys in the Indian contingent.Tariyal's journey into combat sports began not with dreams of an Asian Games medal, but with a desire for self-defence.At 12, after experiencing eve-teasing, she decided she wanted to learn how to fight. She took up judo and gradually transformed that initial need for protection into a competitive sporting career.Judo became her foundation. She trained at the Jawaharlal Nehru Stadium and later at the Dada Dev Mandir Centre in Palam before honing her skills at the Sports Authority of India centre in Bhopal.The journey eventually produced eight national judo titles and international success. She won gold at the 2019 Commonwealth Judo Championships and the 2019 South Asian Games, besides winning silver at the 2018 Commonwealth Judo Championships. She represented India at the 2022 Commonwealth Games in Birmingham in the women's 57kg category, narrowly missing a medal.But judo was only the beginning.Tariyal moved into kurash and represented India at the 2023 Asian Games. She also took up Ju-Jitsu, eventually becoming world champion in the Adults Ju-Jitsu Contact Female 63kg category at the 2024 JJIF Ju-Jitsu World Championships.Her relationship with MMA had begun earlier, with a debut victory in 2017. She then spent seven years away from the sport while continuing her career in other combat disciplines.When she returned to professional MMA in 2024, she did so with the experience of a fighter who had already spent years building different parts of her game.She made her professional comeback at BRAVE CF 92 in Bahrain in December 2024 and won. Her subsequent MMA career included national titles and bronze medals at the Asian Mixed Martial Arts Championships in 2026.That multi-discipline background became central to her Asian Games campaign.Tariyal's MMA style was built around the skills she had accumulated over the years — takedowns, grappling, ground control and submissions.Before the Asian Games, she underwent a six-week preparation camp in Mumbai under coaches Nikhil and Sushobhan. She had spoken about how her coaches would wait for her through Mumbai's traffic so she could complete her training and continue refining her techniques.Her preparation showed when she stepped into the Asian Games cage.In Sunday's quarterfinal, Tariyal defeated Mongolia's Altanchimeg Baigalmaa 2-0 in the women's traditional 60kg category to reach the semifinals. The victory guaranteed India its first medal in MMA because both losing semifinalists received bronze.It was a moment Tariyal had waited years for.“It took me a lot of time to reach here. There is a lot of hard work -- first judo, then other games and now MMA,” she had said after reaching the last four.On Monday, she came within one step of turning that historic bronze into a shot at gold.Instead, the semifinal became a contest decided not simply by what happened inside the cage, but by what the morning weigh-in showed.There is no taking away what Tariyal has accomplished.She has become India's first Asian Games MMA medallist at an edition in which the sport itself is making its debut. At 36, she has added another major milestone to a career that has crossed judo, kurash, Ju-Jitsu and professional MMA.But the circumstances of the semifinal mean the bronze is unlikely to feel complete to her immediately.The Indian challenge had changed the original decision. The bout had become a draw. Tariyal had fought back after losing the opening period and forced the contest into an additional round.Yet the final tiebreak went against her because she was heavier by approximately 700 grams.So the fighter who once took up judo simply because she wanted to learn how to defend herself now stands on an Asian Games podium — but with the memory of a final that was within reach and slipped away on the narrowest of margins.The bronze is historic. The heartbreak is equally real.
Article Summary: MMA is making its Asian Games debut at Aichi-Nagoya 2026. Tariyal's bronze is India's first-ever medal in the discipline. The 36-year-old broke down in tears on the mat after the final decision.

Article Title: How Patrick Mahomes' kids' names - Sterling, Bronze, and Golden tell a hidden story about his career
Article Text:
Patrick Mahomes' kids' names - Sterling, Bronze, and Golden tell a hidden story (Getty Images)

Why did Patrick and Brittany Mahomes choose metal-themed names for their kids?

Do Patrick Mahomes' kids' names reflect his Super Bowl legacy?

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Patrick Mahomes and his wife Brittany are parents to three kids -- Sterling Skye, Patrick "Bronze" Lavon Mahomes III, and Golden Raye, who arrived in January 2025. To most people, these are just unique names. But look a little closer and a pattern appears -- one that connects directly to the metals that define athletic achievement, and quietly mirrors the arc of one of the NFL's most decorated careers.The metallic naming tradition in the Mahomes household did not begin with children. It started with dogs. While still in college, Patrick gifted Brittany a pit bull named Steel -- a nod to the Pittsburgh Steelers. They later added another dog named Silver. By the time their first child came along, the theme had already taken root.Sterling Skye arrived in February 2021, just as Mahomes was cementing himself as one of the most dangerous quarterbacks in the league. Sterling — a reference to sterling silver -- carries a meaning that goes beyond decoration. The word itself signals genuine quality. Something that holds its value. For a quarterback who had already won a Super Bowl MVP before turning 25, the timing felt fitting, even if unintentional.Bronze followed in November 2022, and the story behind that name is more personal. Mahomes has said they were originally going to name their son Trey, since he was Patrick Lavon Mahomes III. It was his brother Jackson who pushed for something different. "He can have his own thing now, where he's not Patrick, he's Bronze," Mahomes explained. The nickname stuck, and with it came an identity separate from the weight of a famous last name.Then came Golden Raye in January 2025 -- the newest member of a family that now numbers five. Gold, in any context, sits at the top. It is the standard everything else gets measured against.The connection is hard to ignore. Sterling, Bronze, Golden -- the three metals of the Olympic podium, and the three children of an athlete who has built one of sport's most dominant dynasties. Whether Mahomes intended it that way is another matter, but the symbolism lands.Laurie Kramer, a professor of applied psychology at Northeastern University, noted that names like these carry dual purpose. "The intention was to build unity in the family," she said. "Everybody's got a metal name in some way, so these kids would feel connected, and it was helping build a family identity around metals which could convey strength and resilience." But Kramer also flagged something worth thinking about: metals come with a built-in ranking. Gold outranks silver. Silver outranks bronze. "When you get names that come with a built-in hierarchy like gold, silver, and bronze, there may be some unintended side effects," she said.Brittany Mahomes has spoken openly about how each name felt right at the time. Sterling was set before they even knew the baby's gender. Bronze evolved naturally once the decision was made to keep the Mahomes name going into a third generation.Golden completed the trio.Together, the three names do something accidental but compelling -- they trace a quiet narrative of a career still being written. Sterling for the early proof of brilliance. Bronze for the continuity of legacy. And Golden, the latest and perhaps most loaded, arriving just as the question of where Mahomes lands all time is being asked more seriously than ever.
Article Summary: Patrick Mahomes and his wife Brittany have three kids -- Sterling Skye, Patrick "Bronze" Lavon Mahomes III, and Golden Raye. Sterling, Bronze, Golden -- the three metals of the Olympic podium, and the three children of an athlete who has built one of sport's most dominant dynasties.

Article Title: “To make sure that our educational system is improved”: How Xavier Worthy is using his Chiefs platform to uplift Kansas City children through education, mentorship and community work
Article Text:
How Xavier Worthy is using his Chiefs platform to uplift Kansas City children through education, mentorship and community work(Getty)

How did Xavier Worthy support Kansas City’s education effort?

How has Xavier Worthy carried that work into his foundation?

Xavier Worthy is known around Kansas City for his speed, big plays and the excitement he brings to the Chiefs. Away from game days, he has also spent time working with children, supporting education programmes and creating opportunities for young people.In April 2026, Worthy helped open the 2026 Charter School Board Draft at Arrowhead Stadium. Hosted by BLAQUE Kansas City, the event brought 15 community leaders together with 10 charter schools looking to fill open board positions. The programme gives local leaders a direct role in helping shape their schools and had placed about 50 community leaders on charter school boards since it began in 2022.Worthy’s role at the April 11 event was to help open the programme. The focus remained on bringing community leaders into Kansas City’s education system and giving schools stronger local representation.Kimberlyn Jones, BLAQUE Kansas City’s director of programme strategy and impact, explained the organisation’s goal:“We are unapologetically determined and driven to make sure that our educational system is improved, that our education system is represented well with the children in the community.”The event followed a draft-style format, matching community leaders with charter schools that had board openings. Worthy’s appearance brought attention to an initiative centred on students, school leadership and the people living in the communities those schools serve.His next major youth event in Kansas City put him directly in front of children.On May 30, 2026, Worthy hosted a free Dream B1G Football Camp at Southeast High School. The camp welcomed 350 children in grades 3 through 8, with participants taking part in football drills, speed training and mentorship.Worthy explained the purpose of the camp: “Just to show them there’s another way,” Worthy said. “Giving them an outlet, whether that’s football, whether that’s showing you can be good at something elseWorthy’s work with young people extends beyond Kansas City through The Worthy 1’s Foundation. The organisation focuses on single mothers and youth and supports programmes involving education, financial assistance, health and wellness, mentorship and sports.His connection to the foundation is rooted in his upbringing. Worthy was raised in Fresno, California, by his mother, Nicky Jones, and the foundation identifies single mothers and young people as the centre of its mission.In July 2025, Worthy returned to Fresno for a free football camp at Edison High School, where he had played as a young athlete. His foundation said more than 400 children attended. The event included football activities, coaching and mentorship, while Worthy spoke about his own path from Fresno to the NFL He also visited King Elementary School during the trip and spoke with students about his journey.The Fresno visit included a personal family moment as well. Worthy threw out the ceremonial first pitch at a Fresno Grizzlies game and recreated an old childhood photograph with his mother and younger sister. A silent auction and jersey raffle were also held to support his foundation’s work with youth and single-parent households.Worthy has now brought that same connection with young people into his life in Kansas City. The April education event placed him alongside community leaders working with charter schools. The May football camp put him in front of hundreds of local children. His foundation continues to focus on young people and single mothers.As a Chiefs receiver, who is still building his NFL career, Worthy is also creating a record of what he wants to give back. His football career brought him to Kansas City. His community work is giving him another way to connect with the people who live there.
Article Summary: Xavier Worthy is using his Chiefs platform to uplift Kansas City children. He has spent time working with children, supporting education programmes and creating opportunities for young people. In April 2026, Worthy helped open the 2026 Charter School Board Draft at Arrowhead Stadium. His next major youth event in Kansas City put him directly in front of children.

Luka Doncic shares honest take on his growth on and off the court

Luka Doncic left basketball out of his newest Instagram post and wrote to his two daughters instead. He shared it on Sunday, after spending a big part of the offseason in Slovenia and getting back to Los Angeles.The note was short and carried no news about the team. Even so, the calendar gives it weight. Lakers media day is Sept. 28, and training camps around the league open the next day. The Slovenian picked his family as the audience before any of that began, and he kept the words plain.The Sept. 20 post was written in Slovenian. Translated into English, its main line reads: “Wherever I go, you are always with me. I love you!”G+O, the daughters' initials, sits at the top of the caption. Doncic also told them that being apart will not change where they stand in his life. Two heart emojis wrap it up. Nothing in it points to the season or his workouts. It reads like a dad checking in, and little else.His daughters were already part of his summer plans. As Reuters reported in May, he chose to skip Slovenia's national-team duty to have more time with them. The 2025-26 season had ended without him on the floor for the playoffs, since a left hamstring injury sidelined him.The Lakers star also used Ljubljana as a small training base. In August, he brought teammates together there for bonding and a pair of casual practices. September brought his own conditioning and court work in the same city. The August meetups gave the group a head start on familiarity before the official preseason.Coach JJ Redick will soon start testing how the roster works around Doncic, and the rotation will take shape from there.Doncic enters this season as the lone headliner in Los Angeles, with LeBron James gone. In an interview with SLAM, he talked about how he has changed. His answer was modest, “probably a better basketball player, more mature.” The way he plays, smile included, is much the same, he added.Madrid is where his pro career started. From there he moved to the NBA and was ranked among its best in short order. Going pro early was not easy, yet he credits it with pushing him to mature faster than most players.Dallas is part of the growth story as well. Boston beat the Mavericks in the 2024 NBA Finals, and Doncic was the one leading Dallas there. Doubts about his leadership, and about whether he could win a title, followed.Los Angeles has already seen the fun side. In one full season with the Lakers, fans and teammates noticed his lively personality, the way he needles opponents and hunts for any competitive edge.

Article Title: 'Age is just a number': Ex-India chief selector Chetan Sharma backs Rohit Sharma to continue playing ODIs
Article Text:
Rohit Sharma (ANI Photo)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

MUMBAI: For the last year or so, Rohit Sharma has gone into every series with growing speculation over his future. The departure of current chief selector Ajit Agarkar - which will become official after October 4, the last date of his tenure - has again turned the spotlight on the former India skipper. It is widely believed that Agarkar's fallout with the BCCI on Rohit's future could be the catalyst in the former India and Mumbai pacer not seeking an extension of his tenure. On September 3, after a review meeting at its headquarters in Mumbai, BCCI secretary Devajit Saikia once again sought to quash the uncertainty around Rohit's ODI future.Amidst a raging debate on the issue, former India pacer and chief selector Chetan Sharma has given a thumbs-up to the 39-year-old Rohit continuing to wear India's ODI jersey."I can understand that people are saying a hundred things. I have been a cricketer too, so I respect and love them as cricketers. Rohit Sharma and Virat Kohli are the 'Kohinoors' of Indian cricket . Age is just a number. If they are good, then why not (can they continue). I myself was a selector. Rohit recently scored a century (138 against England at Lord's in third ODI on July 19). Virat, every game he gets one. Then what is the problem? We want players who can win games for us, and they both are capable of doing it," Sharma told TOI on Monday.Sharma, the first bowler to take a hat-trick in ODI World Cup history (in 1987 against New Zealand at Nagpur), confessed that he was a big fan of the superstar batters."I love watching them when they come and bat for India and they win trophies for us. Rohit won us a trophy after so many years (when he captained India to their second T20 World Cup triumph, and first in 17 years). We should be grateful. We should not listen to other people," Sharma stressed, while talking at an event in Mumbai.Asked specifically if he wished Rohit and Kohli to play in the ODI World Cup next year, Sharma, who played 23 Tests and 65 ODIs from 1984-94, picking up 128 wickets, replied by saying, "If they are fit, they are getting the runs, then why not? I am asking this question to everyone."Considering that presently, Agarkar is apparently not keen to continue because of differences on Rohit's international future, how would Sharma, who was India's chief selector from Dec 2020-Feb 2023, have handled the situation had he been in Agarkar's place? "I won't go into that. When I was the chief selector, we made Rohit the captain. We trusted him, that's why we made him the captain. Virat was always an asset for Indian cricket. As I said, if they are fit, they are getting runs for India, then we should be happy," Sharma asserted.Sharma was pleased that the BCCI has now made it mandatory for all the India players to play domestic cricket as long as they were fit and available. "When I was the India chief selector, my thinking was that if you are doing well in domestic cricket, you should be given a chance. The BCCI spends so much money and effort to organise domestic cricket.We have to respect domestic cricket. Recently, I saw an article that the BCCI told everyone about domestic cricket. So, my dream has come true, and I am really thankful to the BCCI for this. You must play in the Ranji Trophy or first- class cricket if you are fit,” Sharma felt.Sharma, meanwhile, backed both the India women's and men's teams to clinch the gold medal in the 2026 Asian Games in Aichi Nagoya in Japan. The Indian women's team will play Sri Lanka in the gold medal clash on Tuesday, while Shreyas Iyer & Co will launch their campaign in the quarterfinals on September 28.

Rohit recently scored a century (138 against England at Lord's in third ODI on July 19). Virat, every game he gets one. Then what is the problem? We want players who can win games for us, and they both are capable.

Article Title: Wrestler-actor Saurav Gurjar arrested in sexual exploitation case over marriage promise in Hyderabad
Article Text:
Wrestler-actor Saurav Gurjar was arrested at Mumbai airport for alleged sexual exploitation.





HYDERABAD: Wrestler-cum-actor Saurav Gurjar was arrested by Gachibowli police at Mumbai airport for allegedly sexually exploiting a 29-year-old woman on the promise of marriage. He was sent to 14-day judicial remand on Sunday.According to police, the 29-year-old complainant from Nanakramguda alleged that she first connected with Gurjar (40) on Instagram in 2021. They became intimate after their first meeting on Dec 25, 2021, she claimed.“During the course of our relationship, the accused disclosed that he was already married. He repeatedly promised to give me wife-like rights and eventually settle down with me,” the woman stated in her complaint.She alleged that during their five-year relationship, while she stayed with Gurjar at different places in the US and India, he frequently avoided her and even went incommunicado.“He used to block me on the phone/social media and disappear without any prior information. I suffered mental harassment, emotional distress and financial loss, including losing my job after I left my employment in the US to stay with him,” the complainant alleged.According to the woman, Gurjar later helped her relocate to Hyderabad.“She claimed to have relocated with the expectation that they would settle together. But the accused again failed to honour his assurances. He allegedly continued the relationship by making false promises of marriage and subjected her to harassment and sexually exploited her,” Gachibowli police stated in the FIR.Based on the complaint, Gachibowli police registered a case against Gurjar on Aug 15 under Section 69 of the BNS (sexual intercourse by employing deceitful means, etc.).“We also issued a Look Out Circular (LOC) against him. On the night of Sept 17, he was intercepted by immigration officials at Mumbai airport when he arrived from West Asia. Our team brought him to Hyderabad on Saturday and was produced before a magistrate, who remanded him to judicial custody on Sunday,” Gachibowli inspector K Saidulu said.
Article Summary: Wrestler-cum-actor Saurav Gurjar was arrested by Gachibowli police at Mumbai airport. He was sent to 14-day judicial remand on Sunday. The 29-year-old complainant from Nanakramguda alleged that she first connected with Gurjar on Instagram in 2021.

Article Title: Pet Test Incident: Home Guard aspirant dies during physical test; 3rd death in a week in western UP
Article Text:
(Representative image) A 27-year-old Home Guard aspirant died during a physical test in Moradabad





MEERUT: A 27-year-old Home Guard aspirant from Bareilly died after collapsing during a physical efficiency test (PET) at the 9th Battalion PAC ground in Moradabad on Friday, marking the third death in the ongoing recruitment drive in western Uttar Pradesh within a week.Shivam Yadav, a resident of Bareilly city, fell unconscious about 50m from the finish line while running the 12th and final lap of the mandatory 4.8-km race. He was taken to a hospital, where doctors declared him dead, officials said.His father, Vinod Yadav, said he reached the ground after learning that his son’s condition had deteriorated mid-race but was stopped at the gate by police personnel and alleged that he was not allowed inside despite repeated pleas. “By the time I was let in, Shivam had already collapsed,” he said.Shivam’s wife, Komal, said the family had not imagined that the test would cost him his life. The couple had been married for five years and have a toddler daughter.A BTech and BEd graduate who had also cleared the UP-Teacher Eligibility Test (TET), Shivam ran a coaching centre. He had cleared the preliminary and main examinations for railway loco pilot recruitment and was awaiting the results of the Lekhpal and Railway Group D examinations, his family said.He is survived by his parents, wife, daughter and three brothers.In Meerut, two other aspirants died in a similar fashion earlier this week. Shamli resident Ankuj Malik, 39, collapsed on Tuesday after his condition deteriorated following the PET at Kailash Prakash Sports Stadium. Another aspirant, Tarun Kumar, also died this week after falling ill during the run. All three candidates were suspected to have died of cardiac arrest.Meanwhile, two candidates at Bareilly’s Dorilal Stadium — Surjeet Singh and Yuvraj — were hospitalised on Saturday after one collapsed and the other sustained a leg injury, officials said.Neither Moradabad nor Meerut police have shared any details in the three cases. Attempts to reach Moradabad SSP Satpal Antil and Meerut SSP BBGTS Murthy for comment were unsuccessful.
Article Summary: Shivam Yadav, a resident of Bareilly city, fell unconscious about 50m from the finish line while running the 12th and final lap of the mandatory 4.8-km race. He was taken to a hospital, where doctors declared him dead. His father alleged that he was not allowed inside despite repeated pleas.

Article Title: Aamir Khan’s Arjuna-winning ‘coach’ fights to save Indore akhada
Article Text:
Young wrestlers at Indore's Malhar Ashram train amidst severe infrastructure decay.





INDORE: Kripa Shankar Bishnoi’s wards unwittingly had a new routine added to their training regimen this monsoon: bailing bucketfuls of rainwater out of their akhada at Indore’s Malhar Ashram before taking the mat to hone their technique.The Arjuna-winning coach, who trained actor Aamir Khan for his portrayal of Mahavir Phogat in the 2016 blockbuster Dangal, is now struggling to keep his batch of young talents from leaving out of frustration over the worsening state of their training centre.The leaks on the roof of Malhar Ashram centre have got larger for want of repairs, its walls are shedding plaster and the training equipment is constantly at risk of being damaged by puddles forming inside after each downpour.More than 80 wrestlers have been training at Sports Authority of India centre housed at Indore’s Malhar Ashram since 2008. The centre offers free coaching and Bishnoi is always eager to mentor whoever aspires to be a champion wrestler.What he is unable to fix is the state of the structure. “The wrestlers have to clear the puddles that form inside. The situation was particularly worse this year, making it almost impossible for my wrestlers to train properly,” Bishnoi told TOI.With the akhada becoming unusable on days when it rains long and heavily, the centre approached the principal of the adjacent Sandipani Govt Malhar Ashram School this year. The latter opened the school’s unused old boys’ association hall as a stopgap option for about a month.A leaking roof isn’t Bishnoi’s only challenge. SAI centre has no changing room and its toilets are in bad shape, affecting women wrestlers the most. They are forced to use public toilets nearby or knock on the doors of neighbouring houses. A toilet built with local MLA Golu Shukla’s assistance is yet to function.“The centre was originally established as a boarding-cum-wrestling facility but later turned into a day-boarding centre. It is currently functioning without an official SAI coach,” said Bishnoi, who also trained Aamir’s reel daughters, playing the Phogat sisters, in Dangal.The 18-year-old centre has operated without an official coach since it opened. While Bishnoi has chosen to unselfishly mentor aspiring grapplers without access to basic infrastructure or resources, his spirit is close to breaking.“Rainwater mixed with sewer runoff from damaged lines has reached the premises of the training centre,” the Arjuna awardee said. “I raised the issue with chief minister Mohan Yadav. Let’s see what happens.”In a city where traditional akhadas have nurtured generations of wrestlers, including national and international medal-winners, Malhar Ashram’s crumbling training centre awaits an escape from the chokehold of decay.
Article Summary: Kripa Shankar Bishnoi trained actor Aamir Khan for his portrayal of Mahavir Phogat in the 2016 blockbuster Dangal. The Arjuna-winning coach is now struggling to keep his batch of young talents from leaving out of frustration over the worsening state of their training centre.

Article Title: Woman choked with dupatta at Bengaluru home, robbed of gold and cash worth Rs 5.3 lakh
Article Text:
An intruder attacked a homemaker by entering through a first-floor window (Representative image generated using AI)





BENGALURU: A 29-year-old homemaker stepped out of her bathroom to a nightmare when an intruder grabbed her from behind and choked her with a dupatta after entering her Peenya 2nd Stage home through a first-floor window.She lost consciousness during the attack and, on recovering, found her 50-gram gold mangalya chain, worth around Rs 5 lakh, was missing.The miscreant also broke open a wardrobe and took away Rs 30,000 in cash.According to a complaint filed by Kavya (name changed), the incident occurred around 12.30pm on Sept 17, when she was home alone as her husband, a private firm employee, had gone to attend a housewarming ceremony of their relative and their five-year-old daughter was at school.After finishing the house chores, Kavya wanted to take a bath. She said she went to the ground floor of the house and locked all the doors and windows. Then she went to the first floor of the house and locked the door from inside before going to the bathroom to bathe. She had left a window next to the door slightly open.Soon after finishing her bath, she stepped out of the bathroom.The woman said she was grabbed from behind by an unidentified man.He asked her not to make noise or retort and said he would leave after taking whatever he wanted from the house.Kavya said the attacker squeezed her neck with his hands. When she was finding it difficult to breathe, the miscreant took a dupatta and wrapped it around her neck, tightening and twisting it while again warning her not to scream.Kavya told police that she lost consciousness. When she recovered, she realised that her gold mangalya chain was missing.She also found the almirah locker broken open and Rs 30,000 was missing.Her husband and his father soon arrived and rushed her to a nearby private hospital, where the doctors admitted her as an inpatient.Based on the medico-legal case (MLC) report, Byadarahalli police rushed to the hospital and took a complaint from the woman.A senior officer said the miscreant was detained Sunday evening and was being subjected to questioning.
Article Summary: A 29-year-old homemaker stepped out of her bathroom to a nightmare when an intruder grabbed her from behind and choked her. She lost consciousness during the attack and, on recovering, found her 50-gram gold mangalya chain, worth around Rs 5 lakh, was missing. The miscreant also broke open a wardrobe and took away Rs 30,000 in cash.

Article Title: Bill Gates said his children will inherit ‘less than 1%’ of his wealth; ex-wife Melinda Gates is making sure of it, reveals why she didn’t fund daughter's startup
Article Text:
Bill Gates said his children will inherit ‘less than 1%’ of his wealth; ex-wife Melinda Gates is making sure of it, reveals why she didn’t fund daughter's startup

Why Melinda French Gates did not fund her daughter’s startup

Bill Gates said his children will inherit less than 1%

Bill Gates daughter Phoebe launched Phia shopping app

Melinda French Gates says rejection can help female founders

Bill Gates has said his children will inherit less than 1% of his wealth when he dies, and his ex-wife Melinda French Gates appears to be following a similar approach when it comes to helping their children build careers. In a 2025 interview, French Gates revealed that she deliberately stayed out of her daughter Phoebe Gates’ startup fundraising, even though she could have easily opened doors through her vast network. Instead, she watched from the sidelines as her daughter tried to raise money from investors. “She got capitalized not because of my contacts, not because of me. I wouldn’t put money into it,” French Gates said. Her reason was simple: if the startup was a real business, she wanted other investors to believe in it too.French Gates discussed the decision at the Power of Women’s Sports Summit last year, where she explained why she chose not to invest in her daughter’s company.“She got capitalized not because of my contacts, not because of me. I wouldn’t put money into it,” she said.French Gates said she wanted her daughter to experience the fundraising process herself, including the possibility of being rejected by investors.“If this is a real business,” she said, others should be willing to back it.“That’s what I told her,” French Gates added. “She’s growing from this.”Melinda French Gates’ approach echoes a decision Bill Gates has spoken about in the past. The Microsoft cofounder has said his children will receive less than 1% of his fortune after his death. Gates has argued that giving children an extremely large inheritance would not necessarily be helpful and that they should make their own way.French Gates' decision not to invest directly in her daughter's company follows a similar principle. Rather than using her own wealth or contacts to help secure funding, she wanted her daughter to build the company independently.Bill Gates’ youngest daughter Phoebe Gates, has launched a fashion-tech startup called Phia with her Stanford roommate, Sophia Kianni. Phia is a platform that compares clothing prices across more than 40,000 websites, allowing shoppers to search for deals.In April 2025, Phoebe Gates, who was then 22, said her parents had not allowed her to leave Stanford to build a startup, despite her father having taken a different path when he launched Microsoft.The startup has since attracted attention, including recent scrutiny over claims about sales attributed to the platform.For French Gates, the decision was also connected to the challenges faced by women building companies. “It is very, very hard to get your business funded if you’re a woman,” she said. “And so you do have to learn a bit how to have the courage to play the game and to stick with it.”French Gates said resilience is a common quality among successful women featured on her YouTube series, Moments That Make Us.“I saw that going through something difficult changed all of them, and that they had to learn to find resilience somewhere,” she said. “And in finding that resilience, they found themselves.”
Article Summary: Melinda French Gates said she deliberately stayed out of her daughter Phoebe Gates’ startup fundraising. She said she wanted her daughter to experience the fundraising process herself, including the possibility of being rejected by investors. French Gates' decision not to invest directly in her daughter's company follows a similar principle.

El Rubius reflects on a tough and “unfair” exit

Soon after his elimination, the Spanish creator shared a raw reaction with fans, giving them a closer look at what the experience felt like from inside the game. Some viewers believe intense competitions like this naturally lead to uneven situations. Others feel Rubius may have had a point about being singled out.
